name: Sirius Satellite Radio (Tundra)
tagline: Only commercial Tundra-orbit fleet — 3 satellites, 24-hour HEO over North America
description: Commercial satellite-radio constellation in the 24-hour Tundra orbit (~25,000 × 35,786 km) at the 63.4° critical inclination. Each satellite dwells over CONUS for roughly two-thirds of every orbit, giving urban-canyon receivers elevation angles a geostationary signal can't match. Sirius FM-1 launched from Baikonur in 2000 on a Proton-K; the company merged with XM Radio in 2008 to form Sirius XM.
best_known_for: 24-hour Tundra HEO — apogee dwells ~16 hours per day over North America
